articles.title: Why developing a love for reading is one of the greatest things for your dev career
articles.excerpt: I'm just starting out on my frontend learning journey right now, and I noticed something while reading about CSS on MDN: I love to read. This is not news to me. Over the last 7 years, I read many fant…
articles.body: I'm just starting out on my frontend learning journey right now, and I noticed something while reading about CSS on MDN: I love to read. This is not news to me. Over the last 7 years, I read many fantasy novels with 500 pages or more, among them series as large as the "Wheel of time" series and the "Stormlight Archives". I love to read. I grew up in a family of readers, and it is one of the things I am most grateful for in my life. But I never realized that it is probably one of the biggest reasons for my success as a software developer as well. In this article, I want to go into the reasons why I think this is true. First, our job is to read and write. Aside from communicating in person or over Zoom calls, that's all we do, day in and day out. This won't even change with AI.

articles.body: Help wanted: validate a SharePoint Requests & Approvals SPFx sample I have opened a new SharePoint Framework sample for a small, list-backed Requests & Approvals inbox: Pull request: https://github.com/pnp/sp-dev-fx-webparts/pull/6475 The sample targets common SMB/SME approval scenarios without introducing a workflow engine or additional service dependencies. articles.title: I Built an AI Agent That Negotiates My Bills For Me, Here's Everything That Went Wrong
articles.excerpt: This post showcases my journey of the All Things Agentic Hackathon. I'm a second semester software engineering student, and a few weeks ago I had an idea I couldn't stop thinking about, what if an AI…
articles.body: This post showcases my journey of the All Things Agentic Hackathon . I'm a second semester software engineering student, and a few weeks ago I had an idea I couldn't stop thinking about, what if an AI agent could actually haggle on my behalf, the way I never have the nerve to on a retention call? That idea became Haggle, an agent that researches real competitor pricing, then negotiates round by round against a second AI playing a subscription service's retention department, until it lands a deal or walks away. Built on Gemini 3.5 Flash, Google ADK 2.0, and the A2A (Agent-to-Agent) protocol, for the All Things Agentic Hackathon's Taskmaster track . The idea took an afternoon. Getting it actually working took a lot longer, and almost none of the hard parts were about AI.

articles.title: Beyond the Cloud Bound: Why Local-First and Client-Side Privacy Are the Developer's New OS
articles.excerpt: Originally published on tamiz.pro. Look around the modern developer's desktop. It is cluttered with floating panels that whisper, listen, and watch. They promise to revolutionize our workflows through…
articles.body: Originally published on tamiz.pro . The Leash Is Tightening Look around the modern developer's desktop. It is cluttered with floating panels that whisper, listen, and watch. They promise to revolutionize our workflows through AI, but at what cost? We have traded the efficiency of code generation for the surrender of our data sovereignty. We have accepted the latency of round-trips to distant data centers as the tax we pay for intelligence. But as we move from autonomous agents to true autonomy, a critical architectural pivot is emerging—one that prioritizes local-first execution and client-side privacy over the seductive convenience of the cloud-bound model.

articles.excerpt: Some imagination and an AI tool is all you need.
articles.body: As someone who grew up in the 90s, I can tell you that ringtones were once a major status symbol. It meant you had a cutting-edge phone capable of such witchcraft, after all. Unfortunately, it took less than a decade for custom ringtones to go from impressive to something most people considered tacky. The rise of smartphones and the bombardment of notifications didn’t help custom ringtones any, either. Even if not as popular as they once were, ringtones are still a great way to add a little flair to your phone, as long as you don’t go overboard. These days, there are tons of sources for ringtones, from dedicated apps to websites that allow you to download ringtone files. Many phones can even take full tunes you own and automatically cut them into ringtones.

articles.title: How to Build a Good Human-in-the-Loop for AI Email and Outbound Messaging
articles.excerpt: A good human in the loop for AI email is more than a confirmation dialog on every draft. You want controls that make a wrong send cheap to undo, cap how far it can reach, and put a real human gate onl…
articles.body: A good human in the loop for AI email is more than a confirmation dialog on every draft. You want controls that make a wrong send cheap to undo, cap how far it can reach, and put a real human gate only on the sends a person can actually catch in time. The question driving all of LoopRails applies here too: can a human realistically catch this mistake before it lands? If the agent is about to send one internal draft, a short undo window beats a click. If it is about to blast 10,000 customers, no human reads fast enough, so you prevent the bad outcome with caps and approval rather than a rubber stamp.

articles.title: Martin Scorsese's Controversial 10/10 Psychological Thriller Is Officially Free on Streaming
articles.excerpt: One of the most engrossing cinematic portraits of urban isolation.
articles.body: The 1970s saw the sudden rise of neo-noir for good reason. Filmmakers like Sydney Pollack and David Lynch brought back classic film noir tropes only to subvert them, introducing a true-to-reality grittiness that reflected the times. These stories were visually distinct with their high-contrast palettes and often featured graphic violence and psychosexual themes while focusing on a complex anti-hero. Films like Chinatown (1974), Blue Velvet (1986), and The Fourth Man (1983) began shaping the genre, marking a shift towards raw urban realism on film, along with the portrayal of tense socio-political backdrops.

articles.title: NASA's Roman Space Telescope is ready for launch aboard SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket
articles.excerpt: A SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket is poised to lift off with the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope on Aug. 30. This observatory is on a mission to usher in a new wave of astronomical discovery.
articles.body: CAPE CANAVERAL, Fla. — A new flagship observatory is about to launch to space and join the ranks of its powerful predecessors, like the Hubble and James Webb space telescopes. NASA's groundbreaking new Nancy Roman Grace Space Telescope is ready to lift off aboard a SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket. It's scheduled to depart from Launch Complex-39A at NASA's Kennedy Space Center in Florida, bound for a gravitationally stable spot in space called Lagrange Point 2, or L2, nearly 1 million miles (1.6 million km) from Earth . The spacecraft's first window for launch is tomorrow (Aug 30) at 7:26 a.m. EDT (1126 GMT). Mission managers and launch administrators held a prelaunch briefing on Saturday (Aug. 29), confirming NASA and SpaceX's "go" to proceed toward tomorrow's lift off.

articles.title: This Week In Space podcast: Episode 225 — Get a Grip!
articles.excerpt: On Episode 225 of This Week In Space, Rod Pyle and Tariq Malik are joined by Adam Kall of KMI to discuss their work on the ISS may provide answers for orbital debris mitigation.
articles.body: On Episode 225 of This Week In Space , Rod Pyle and Tariq Malik are joined by Adam Kall of KMI to discuss their work on the ISS, the goals of the company, and how nature — via the humble octopus and gecko lizards — may provide answers for orbital debris mitigation. The mitigation of orbital debris is an increasingly serious problem that has not gotten enough attention, but this is changing. Commercial companies are addressing orbital debris, and one of them, KMI Space, has flown its experiments aboard the International Space Station, performing over 170 individual rendezvous-and-grab operations. The results are very promising, and the company is moving ahead with ever more ambitious designs. Download or subscribe to this show at: https://twit.tv/shows/this-week-in-space .

articles.title: When is the next lunar eclipse?
articles.excerpt: When will Earth's shadow cover the moon next following the August 2026 partial lunar eclipse?
articles.body: August's "almost Blood Moon" partial lunar eclipse has come and gone, delighting stargazers with a gorgeous natural light show as light filtered by our planet's atmosphere turned it a deep crimson around the point of maximum eclipse. But when is the next lunar eclipse ? Earth won't darken the moon again until Feb. 20, 2027, when a penumbral eclipse will cast our planet's soft outer shadow across February's full "Snow Moon" , so named for the freezing weather that occurs around the time it rises. articles.title: On this day in space! Aug. 29, 1965: NASA's Gemini 5 breaks spaceflight duration record after 2 astronauts spent '8 days in a garbage can'
articles.excerpt: On Aug. 29, 1965, two NASA astronauts returned to Earth after spending eight days in space on the record-setting Gemini 5 mission, setting the stage for longer trips to the moon.
articles.body: On Aug. 29, 1965, two NASA astronauts returned from their record-breaking Gemini 5 mission . Astronauts Gordon Cooper and Pete Conrad spent eight days in Earth orbit, and for the first time, the United States set a world record for the duration of a crewed spaceflight. The Gemini 5 mission launched on Aug. 21, 1965 atop a Titan II rocket from what was then the Cape Canaveral Air Force Station (now the Cape Canaveral Space Force Station ) in Florida. While in orbit, the astronauts were supposed to test rendezvous capabilities and maneuvers using a pod that deployed from their spacecraft. But due to an electrical problem, they had to cancel those plans along with several science experiments.

articles.title: Meeting Nancy Grace Roman: What was the 'mother of Hubble' really like?
articles.excerpt: Nearly a decade ago, I found myself laughing alongside Nancy Grace Roman: one of the most iconic women in astronomy.
articles.body: Nearly a decade ago, I found myself laughing alongside one of the most iconic women in astronomy. This week, a telescope bearing her name launches to the stars . So let's travel back in time and meet Nancy Grace Roman together. Standing under a tent in Washington D.C. at the 2017 inaugural "March for Science," a hodgepodge of scientists and reporters crowd together as the rain pours down outside. "That's Nancy Roman," I hear Bill Nye whisper to me as we stood on the outskirts of the tent. And as I struggled to keep my cool next to one of my childhood heroes, here he is pointing out another. Looking across the room, I see her. There, in the corner of the tent, a woman with white hair wearing a "science not silence" pin sits by herself, soaking in the scenery.

articles.title: ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude quietly get worse over time. This hidden setting fixes them
articles.excerpt: Your favorite AI chatbot might be remembering a little too much.
articles.body: I’ve been using LLM-based AI in some capacity for roughly half a decade, and in that time, the industry has changed significantly. Not only have newer competitors like Gemini and Claude arrived on the scene, but older tools like ChatGPT have also evolved dramatically. We’ve seen better third-party app integration, increased reasoning capabilities, and countless other advancements. However, I would argue that the ability to retain memories matters most. Retaining context from previous conversations helps the AI better anticipate your needs within a single session. It also allows the tool to learn more about you, ensuring that future conversations are tailored to your preferences. However, there is a real downside to memory accumulation that not everyone considers.
